title: Ringed-site exceptional evaluation and opposite currying
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\ge1$. Put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. All schemes below are $k$-schemes. Use ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories on small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] and small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], taken small in a larger universe [def-weil-size-convention]. On either site $D^b_{ctf}$ denotes bounded complexes with constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude: tensoring with any degree-zero module sheaf has cohomology in one fixed finite interval [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes, def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude].

Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ be a closed immersion between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. On etale sites write $s=i^*$ for exact constant-coefficient inverse image, $F=Ri_!=Ri_*$ for compact support [def-amb-etale-compact-support], and $G=i^\times$ for its ambient right adjoint [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], with counit $\mu:FG\to\mathrm{id}$. For the structure map $a_T:T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ put $\omega_T=a_T^\times A$ and $\omega_Z=G\omega_T$. Set $D_W=R\mathcal Hom_A(-,\omega_W)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Write $\mathrm{ev}_H:D_WH\otimes_A^LH\to\omega_W$ for evaluation, $\sigma$ for signed tensor symmetry, and $\delta_H:H\to D_WD_WH$ for the transpose of $\mathrm{ev}_H\sigma_{H,D_WH}$ [lem-weil-duality-pairing].

Assume $s,G$ and $D_W$ preserve the indicated $D^b_{ctf}$ subcategories. Assume the canonical projection transformation $FB\otimes_A^LM\to F(B\otimes_A^LsM)$ [def-kun-projection-formula-map] is invertible for $B\in D^b_c(Z_e,A)$ and $M\in D^b_{ctf}(T_e,A)$.

On each of these ringed sites there is a natural derived tensor-Hom isomorphism
$$R\mathcal Hom(B_0,R\mathcal Hom(C_0,H))\cong R\mathcal Hom(B_0\otimes_A^LC_0,H)$$
for arbitrary $B_0,C_0,H$ in the ordinary derived category. It induces the natural adjunction $\operatorname{Hom}(B_0,R\mathcal Hom(C_0,H))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(B_0\otimes_A^LC_0,H)$, whose counit is evaluation. Its tensor symmetry is induced by $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{\deg x\deg y}y\otimes x$ and is involutive.

For $M,N\in D^b_{ctf}(T_e,A)$ let $q_{M,N}:sM\otimes_A^LGN\to G(M\otimes_A^LN)$ be the exceptional-adjunction transpose of
$$F(sM\otimes_A^LGN)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{PF}^{-1}}M\otimes_A^LFGN\xrightarrow{1\otimes\mu_N}M\otimes_A^LN,$$
where $\mathrm{PF}$ is the assumed projection map conjugated by the displayed tensor symmetries. Then $q$ is natural in both variables. For $K\in D^b_{ctf}(T_e,A)$ define
$$r_K=G(\mathrm{ev}_K\sigma_{K,D_TK})q_{K,D_TK}\sigma_{GD_TK,sK},\qquad\alpha_K=\operatorname{transpose}(r_K):GD_TK\to D_ZsK.$$
For every $L\in D^b_{ctf}(T_e,A)$ put $P=sD_TL$, $U=GL$, $c_L=\alpha_{D_TL}G\delta_L$, and $b_L=G(\mathrm{ev}_L)q_{D_TL,L}:P\otimes_A^LU\to\omega_Z$. These specified morphisms satisfy
$$\mathrm{ev}_P(c_L\otimes1_P)=b_L\sigma_{U,P}:U\otimes_A^LP\to\omega_Z.$$
Here composition is read right to left, and $\omega_Z=G\omega_T$ throughout. This identity does not require $\alpha$ or $\delta$ to be invertible.

proof.text: Use the existing ordinary derived tensor and its parameterized internal-Hom adjunction on each site. For any test object V, conjugate the tensor-Hom Hom equivalence by the specified signed symmetry to put the tensor argument on the right. Its naturality follows from the adjunction naturality and the naturality of the specified symmetry. Its inverse-transpose formula is tensoring the map with the identity followed by the swapped counit. The canonical derived symmetry is involutive by the already proved derived symmetric-category structure [lem-asd-derived-category-symmetric]. No boundedness or constructibility condition is used.

source.place: Second paragraph; formal adjunction calculation, with Stacks sites-cohomology lemma-internal-hom (08J9) and lemma-symmetric-monoidal-derived (0FPT).

proof.text: Apply the right-order Hom equivalence twice, precompose by the inverse associator and apply the inverse right-order Hom equivalence for B tensor C. This gives Hom(V,H(B,H(C,W))) equivalent to Hom(V,H(B tensor C,W)). Associator naturality in V proves that this equivalence is natural in V. Yoneda full faithfulness [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] gives the representing isomorphism. The resulting hom postcomposition equals this explicit equivalence. Applying the same Hom equivalence to the desired parameter squares reduces naturality in B and C to associator naturality in the middle and right arguments, and naturality in W to adjunction naturality. The equivalence definition gives the required arbitrary-test normalization equation. Specialize to each of the two ordinary derived sheaf categories on T and Z.

source.place: Second paragraph; formal adjunction calculation, with Stacks sites-cohomology lemma-internal-hom (08J9) and lemma-symmetric-monoidal-derived (0FPT).

proof.text: Use the stored projection_left and projection_right equations in the canonical boundary data [def-weil-boundary-data]. Cancel the invertible projection components to obtain the corresponding inverse-projection equations. Expand q as its exceptional-adjunction transpose. Adjunction naturality, the two symmetry naturalities, inverse-projection naturality and counit naturality prove separately naturality of q in its first and second variable. Composing these equations and using functoriality of G proves the two-variable equation in Conclusions.

source.place: Second paragraph; formal adjunction calculation, with Stacks sites-cohomology lemma-internal-hom (08J9) and lemma-symmetric-monoidal-derived (0FPT).

proof.text: Uncurry alpha using its explicit definition in [def-weil-boundary-data]. The inverse tensor-Hom equivalence cancels its transpose. Cancel the two consecutive source symmetries and the two consecutive target symmetries using the stored involution laws. What remains is q followed by G of the tensor-Hom counit. Put DL=H(L,W) and delta=transpose(evaluation(W,L)). The tensor-Hom counit equation says (identity_DL tensor delta) followed by that counit is evaluation(W,L).

source.place: Second paragraph; formal adjunction calculation, with Stacks sites-cohomology lemma-internal-hom (08J9) and lemma-symmetric-monoidal-derived (0FPT).

proof.text: Apply right-order uncurrying to the left side of OppositeCurrying and use tensor-Hom naturality in the test object. Substitute the alpha formula from the preceding step. Move G(delta) through q by its second-variable naturality from step 3 and combine the two G-maps. The counit equation from step 4 reduces their composite to G(evaluation(W,L)), proving exactly the stated opposite-currying equality. Preservation by G and twice by duality supplies the two invertible projection components. The proof never inverts alpha or delta.
